newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela considers new deep-water oil terminal.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela considers new deep-water oil terminal.

text.p: Venezuela's congressional Environment Committee plans to study the viability of a new deepwater oil export terminal in the Gulf of Venezuela to bypass the narrow Lake Maracaibo shipping channel, the Commission president said on Thursday.
Cesar Perez Vivas said a workshop would be set up in May or June this year.
The announcement follows a 25,000 barrel oil spill in the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel on February 28, when a Greek- flagged tanker ran aground.

"The Commission is investigating the causes of the accident and the possible existence of some object in the area which could cut into the hulls of ships using the shipping channel," Perez told journalists in Congess.
He said he was particularly concerned by the growing salinity of Lake Maracaibo as a result of dredging to allow more oil and coal exports from the region.

"This is why we stressed the importance of discussing the construction of a new deep-water port to the north of the lake on the Gulf of Venezuela for the export of oil, coal and other products," Perez said.
The deep water terminal would be connected by pipeline to the oil producing region further south.
